title: Derived direct image for a morphism of ringed spaces
statement: Let $g=(g,g^\sharp):(X,\mathcal O_X)\to(Y,\mathcal B)$ be a morphism of ringed spaces [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], and let $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$, $\Mod(\mathcal B)$ be the abelian categories of sheaves of modules on the sites of open subsets of $X$ and of $Y$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; these sites are small, as the opens of a space form a set. *Direct image of modules.* For $\mathcal F\in\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ let $g_*\mathcal F$ be the sheaf $V\mapsto\mathcal F(g^{-1}V)$ on $Y$, with the restrictions of $\mathcal F$, made a $\mathcal B$-module by letting $b\in\mathcal B(V)$ act on $\mathcal F(g^{-1}V)$ as $g^\sharp_V(b)\in\mathcal O_X(g^{-1}V)$; for a morphism $\varphi$ put $(g_*\varphi)_V=\varphi_{g^{-1}V}$. This is an additive functor $g_*:\Mod(\mathcal O_X)\to\Mod(\mathcal B)$, applied termwise to complexes; it carries homotopies to homotopies. *Derived direct image.* Let $Q$ denote the localization functors to $D(\mathcal O_X)$ and $D(\mathcal B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. By [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] choose, functorially in the complex $K$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, a K-injective resolution $K\to I(K)$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. The derived direct image $Rg_*:D(\mathcal O_X)\to D(\mathcal B)$ is the functor with $Rg_*(QK)=Q(g_*I(K))$ and $Rg_*(Q f)=Q(g_*I(f))$. It is well defined: if $s:K\to K'$ is a quasi-isomorphism then $I(s)$ is a quasi-isomorphism between K-injective complexes, hence a homotopy equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], so $g_*I(s)$ is a homotopy equivalence and $Q(g_*I(s))$ is invertible; thus $K\mapsto Q(g_*I(K))$ inverts quasi-isomorphisms and factors uniquely through $Q$. For any K-injective resolution $K\to J$ the comparison $I(K)\to J$ (the homotopy class corresponding under [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] to $QI(K)\cong QK\cong QJ$) is a homotopy equivalence, so $Rg_*(QK)\cong Q(g_*J)$: $Rg_*K$ is represented by $g_*J$ for every K-injective resolution $K\to J$.
